newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds track Treasuries lower as resistance holds.
newsitem.headline: Bunds track Treasuries lower as resistance holds.

text.p: German Bunds slid to losses in late trade on Wednesday as sentiment received knocks from a fall in U.S. Treasuries and the market's repeated failure to breach key resistance, dealers said.
"The lack of follow-through buying on the upside combined with weakness in U.S. Treasuries is underpinning bearish sentiment here," one Frankfurt-based dealer said.

December Bund futures closed at 99.15, down 40 basis points from Tuesday's close, and just above the session low of 99.14. The yield on the benchmark, 10-year cash bond rose to 6.05 percent in late trade, up from 5.99 percent on Tuesday.
Expectations of a slowdown in September M3, expected late this week or early next, were an insufficient support for Bunds in view of the decline in U.S. Treasuries.

The 30-year 6-3/4 percent benchmark Treasury bond was quoted down 19/32 at 98-7/32 in midday U.S. trade, its yield rising to 6.89 percent, due to weakening European markets, talk of foreign central bank selling and emerging jitters about upcoming supply, dealers said.
U.S. debt prices fell across the yield curve, as did German debt.
Chartwatchers saw little potential for a rapid Bund recovery. They identified technical support for December Bund futures at 99.10, a breach of which would push the contract to 98.80.
They saw resistance at 99.55 and 99.63. Dealers said they were disappointed by the Bund's failure to breach resistance at 99.70, Wednesday's session high.
